Ligand-Regulated Palladium-Catalyzed Regiodivergent
Hydroarylation of the Distal Double Bond of Allenamides with Aryl
Boronic Acid
Xin Du, † Huan Zhao, † Xinling Li, Lizhi Zhang, Yunhui Dong, Ping Wang, Daopeng Zhang, Qing Liu,
and Hui Liu *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2021, 86, 13276 −13288 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: The ligand-regulated regiodivergent hydroarylation of the
distal double bond of allenamides with aryl boronic acid was achieved in
the presence of palladium(II) catalysts, delivering a variety of function-
alized enamide with excellent E selectivity and Markovnikov/anti-
Markovnikov selectivity. Two possible coordination intermediates were
proposed to be responsible for the regiodivergent hydroarylation: (1) The
coordination Intermediate I , which was proposed to be formed through
the coordination of MeCN, distal double bond, phenyl to palladium, led to
the aryl group away from the Intermediate I , inducing excellent E
selectivity and anti-Markovnikov selectivity. (2) A switch of regioselectivity
to 1,2- Markovnikov hydroarylation was obtained using bidentate
phosphine ligand (dppf or Xantph os). The formed coordination
Intermediate II led to the N-tether away from the Intermediate II and
at the trans position of aryl, resulting in excellent E selectivity and Markovnikov selectivity. Meanwhile, tentative investigation on the
mechanism proved that the hydron source of this hydroarylation is more likely to be boronic acid. The transmetallation between aryl
boronic acid and palladium catalyst was the initial step of this transformation.
■ INTRODUCTION
Regioselective processes to form one major isomer out of the
possible outcomes are sought after in chemistry. 1,2 It is more
attractive to develop regiodivergent reactions to achieve
diﬀerent regioisomers just by appropriately modulating the
reaction conditions.
3 Notably, regiodivergent carbon −carbon
bonds construction is of central importance to form the
desired skeletal backbones.
4
Allenamides, inducing delocalization of the lone pair
electrons on nitrogen and therefore exhibiting improved
stability, are ubiquitous in organic chemistry.
5 Considering
the particular skeleton of allenamide bearing two C −C π
bonds, controlling the site selectivity still constituted a
daunting scenario, reinforcing a change in strategy. 6 On the
basis of our interest in developing selective functionalization of
allenamides,
7 we envision that transition-metal-catalyzed
hydroarylation with high distal double-bond selectivity could
deliver versatile functionalized enamides, which have emerged
as increasingly valuable functional groups and highly useful
building blocks in synthetic chemistry.
8 As predicted, four
isomers might be alternatively products, involving Z/E and
anti-Markovnikov/Markovnikov selectivity ( Figure 1 ). There-
fore, the precise control of the regioselectivity and diaster-
eoselectivity issue remains a signi ﬁcant challenge.
Although a large number of hydroarylation of allenamides
have been described to synthesize substituted alkenes,
9 highly
selective distal hydroarylation to construct enamides is
relatively underdeveloped. In 2007, Fujii and Ohno developed
an Au-catalyzed intramolecular 1,2-anti-Markovnikov hydro-
arylation of allenamides to synthesize dihydroquinolines, which
exhibited a high 6-endo selectivity due to the preferable
stability of six-membered cyclization.
10
In 2010, Kimber demonstrated intermolecular gold-
catalyzed 1,2-anti-Markovnikov hydroarylation of activated
allenamides, during which e lectron-rich aromatics and
heteroaromatics are necessary (Eq. 1, Scheme 1 A).11 Very
recently, Taillefer and Monnier et. al realized a similar
methodology using an additive-free copper catalytic system. 12
Bandini group developed a Ni-catalyzed stereoselective
synthesis of (E)-trisubstituted tertiary enamides via 1,2-
Markovnikov hydroarylation of allenamides using aryl boronic

palladium-catalyzed regioselect ive hydroarylation reaction
relying on a borylation arylation strategy, and the 1,2-
Markovnikov hydroarylation could be achieved via a sequential
procedure by adjusting the addition order of the catalyst and
iodobenzene derivatives (Eq. 3, Scheme 1 A).
14 In all of these
pioneering examples, excellent regioselectivities were achieved;
however, only one regioisomer could be obtained, and no
regiodivergent enantioselective strategy has previously been
reported.
Driven by our special interest in transition-metal-catalyzed
selective functionalization of allenamides, we thus envisioned
whether we could devlop a ligand-regulated palladium-
catalyzed hydroarylation of allenamides with high regio- and
stereoselectivities ( Scheme 1 B). Considering the Pd −phenyl
complex generated from transmetalation of Pd(II) with aryl
boronic acid, a coordination intermediate might be formed via
the coordination of Pd with less steric hindrance ligand, distal
alkene, and N-tether, which could induce E and anti-
Markovnikov selectivity ( Scheme 1 B, bottom).
On the other hand, another coordination intermediate might
be formed through the coordination of a large ligand with
palladium, which will keep the N-tether away from the more
steric hindrance ligand and phenyl group, leading to E and

this idea, we herein wish to report our new achievements on
palladium-catalyzed regiodivergent hydroarylation of allena-
mides with aryl boronic acid regulated through the
coordination intermediates ( Scheme 1 C). The Intermediate
I was proposed to be formed through the coordination of
MeCN, distal double bond, aryl group to palladium, and the
internal steric hindrance of Intermediate I caused the aryl
group far away from the coordination complex, inducing
excellent E selectivity and anti-Markovnikov selectivity
(Scheme 1 C, left).
Then, Intermediate II was formed through coordination of
dppf with Pd-aryl, resulting in the N-tether far away from the
coordination complex and staying at the trans position of the
aryl group, leading to excellent E selectivity and Markovnikov
selectivity ( Scheme 1 C, right).
■ RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
To verify our hypothesis, we tested the hydroarylation using
allenamide 1a and o-chloro phenylboronic acid 2a as the
model substrates. ( Table 1). First of all, considering less steric
hindrance complex, PdCl 2 without additional ligand was
utilized as precatalyst. However, a trace of the desired product
was detected via GCMS (entry 1). We have tested the reaction
with PdCl
2 (10 mol %) and 3 equivalents of CH 3CN.
Unfortunately, the desired product was not detected and no
reaction was performed. When Pd(OAc)
2 was used combined
with K 3PO4 in dioxane, the hydroarylation products were
isolated in a 49% yield. Although the ratio of anti-Markov
addition product 3a to Markov addition product 4a is 49:51,
excellent E selectivity was obtained (entry 3). Notably, the
utilizing of ligand 2,2-dipyridyl could improve the ratio of
3a:4a to 95:5 with a 45% yield (entry 4). To our delight, the
application of Pd(CH
3CN)2Cl2 could provide the desired anti-
Markov addition product 3a in 86% yield with 99:1 selectivity
(3a:4a). Several bases were also investigated, such as Cs 2CO3,
CsF, K 2CO3, and DIPEA; however, no better results were
obtained (see the SI for more details). Furthermore, bidentate
phosphine ligand was investigated to regulate the coordination
via steric hindrance to produce Markovnikov product 4a. The
use of diphosphine ligands such as dppm, dppp, and dppb
provided 3a in medium yields. Importantly, both Xantphos and
dppf provided the desired 4a in good isolated yields and
Markovnikov hydroarylation selectivity. Notably, the rigid
structure of dppf might be more favoring the stability of
coordination intermediate II than the other complex leading
to the good selectivity to 4a. Thus, Pd(CH
3CN)2Cl2/K3PO4
and Pd(OAc)2/DPPF or Xantphos/K 3PO4 were chosen to the

the substrate scope of anti-Markovnikov hydroarylation ( Table

desired products e ﬃciently ( 3g−3l).
Remarkably, the active Br, OTs, and OTf, which could be
further transformed to more valuable molecules via coupling

conditions.
Furthermore, heteroaryl boronic acids (such as bearing
benzofuran, 2,6-di-Cl-pyridine, and 10-phenyl-9,10-dihydroa-
cridine) were also examined and the corresponding products
were obtained in moderate yields with good anti-Markovnikov
hydroarylation selectivity ( 3m−3o). The reaction of (4 ′-
chloro-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)boronic acid with the allenamide
aﬀorded the enamide derivate in 81% yield with 97:3

or -poor substitutions, the transformation of allenamides

in moderate yields ( 3q−3s). Besides Ts-protected allenamide,

Subsequently, we moved to explore the substrate scope of
Markovnikov hydroarylation ( Table 3). First of all, a variety of
halides are well tolerated, including ﬂuoro, chloro, and bromo
(4a−4f). Gratifyingly, aryl boronic acids with both electron-
donating ( 4g−4j) and electron-withdrawing ( 4k−4l) groups
were examined and the transformation proceeded smoothly to
deliver the corresponding Markovnikov products in moderate
to high yields, with good regioselectivity.
In particular, the active group in coupling reactions such as
OTs and Bromo, survived well in this strategy. Furthermore,
pyridyl ( 4m)-, naphthyl ( 4n)-, and biphenyl ( 4o)-substituted
boronic acid successfully a ﬀorded the desired Markovnikov
hydroarylation products in good yields with excellent
selectivity. Two allenamides were also investigated, which
showed good compatibility to this strategy ( 4p−4q).
To get insight into the reaction mechanism, a series of
preliminary mechanistic exploration experiments were per-
formed. First, some controlled experiments were conducted to
investigate the source of hydrogen in this transformation
(Scheme 2). When the reaction was carried out in 1,4-dioxane-
D8, the corresponding anti-Markov addition product 3a−I was
obtained in an 81% yield without deuterium labeling,
indicating that the hydrogen did not originate from solvent
(Scheme 2 a, entry 1). However, when the reaction was
conducted in 1,4-dioxane (2 mL) with D
2O (2.0 equiv),
product 3a−I was isolated in a 47% yield with quite less
deuterium incorporation ( Scheme 2 a, entry 2). This
observation made us speculate that the source of hydrogen is
not from the residual H
2O of solvent but maybe from boronic
acid. Subsequently, 2-(2-chlorophenyl)-4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-
1,3,2-dioxaborolane 5a was synthesized and subjected to the
mixed solvent of 1,4-dioxane (2 mL) and D 2O (2.0 equiv)
under standard condition. Notably, the reaction a ﬀorded
compound 3a−I in 8% yield with less than 5% deuterium
incorporation. ( Scheme 2 b, entry 1). Nevertheless, when the
reaction of 1a and 5a was conducted under the standard
condition, the transformation could not be proceeded ( Scheme
2b, entry 2). On the basis of these results, the hydrogen for

shown in Scheme 3, o-chlorophenylboronic acid 2a was added

Based on the results above, a possible mechanism for this
ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed regiodivergent hydro-
arylation of allenamides with aryl boronic acid was proposed
as depicted in Scheme 5 . In cycle I, transmetalation between
Pd(II) catalyst and o-chlorophenylboronic acid 2a generated
the Pd −phenyl complex B, which then coordinated to
allenamide 1a to form the coordination intermediate I with
MeCN, distal double bond, phenyl of allenamide. The specially
coordinated structure of intermediate I induced excellent E
selectivity and anti-Markovnikov addition selectivity of hydro-
arylation to deliver intermediate C. The following hydro-
genolysis of palladium complex C with the hydrogen from the
aryl boronic acid a ﬀorded the anti-Markovnikov product 3a
with regeneration of L
1-Pd(II) catalyst. On the other hand,
when the large ligand dppf was used, the transmetallation
could generate palladium(II) species D. The coordination of
dppf with complex D formed a complex in which the N-tether
was pushed out of the complex and at the trans position to aryl
group, resulting in excellent E selectivity and Markovnikov
selectivity as depicted in coordination intermediate II .
Meanwhile, intermediate III is sterically disfavored than
intermediate II a ss h o w ni nc y c l e II of Scheme 4 .
Subsequently, the coordination intermediate II underwent
Markovnikov addition to a ﬀord the Pd(II) intermediate E.
Finally, hydrogenolysis of intermediate E gave the desired
product 4a with regeneration of the L
2-Pd(II) catalyst.
■ CONCLUSIONS
Overall, we have developed the palladium-catalyzed regiodi-
vergent hydroarylation of allenamides through ligand regu-
lation. Various allenamides reacted with aryl boronic acids to
produce the corresponding Markovnikov or anti-Markovni-
kov hydroarylation products (functionalized enamide) in high
yields with excellent regioselectivity. Through ligand regu-
lation, the hydroarylation regioselectivity of the distal double
bond of allenamide is controllable.
15 Controlled experiments
on the mechanism indicated that the hydrogen source may
come from boronic acid for the ﬁrst time. Two possible
coordination intermediates were proposed to be responsible
for the excellent E selectivity and Markovnikov/anti-
Markovnikov selectivity: (1) The coordination intermediate
I, which was proposed to be formed through the coordination
of MeCN, distal double bond, phenyl to palladium, led to the
aryl group away from intermediate I , inducing excellent E
selectivity and anti-Markovnikov selectivity. (2) A switch of
regioselectivity to 1,2- Markovnikov hydroarylation was
obtained using bidentate phosphine ligand (dppf or
Xantphos). The formed coordination intermediate II led to
the N-tether away from intermediate II and at the trans
position of aryl, resulting in excellent E selectivity and
Markovnikov selectivity. Further investigation on the mecha-
nism of regiodivergent hydroarylation and application of the
enamides will be in due course.
